entries.target: wine:Jean Foillard ‘Côte du Py’ Morgon 2024 (1.5 L magnum)

value.a:
This magnum is the 2024 Côte du Py from the Foillard domaine in Morgon, a cru Beaujolais, $270 for 1.5 L, bin 12567, printed under Large Formats, Red, France and again on the Beaujolais page.

Morgon, mor-GOHN, is one of the ten crus of Beaujolais, and the Côte du Py, koht dew PEE, is the hill at its center: decomposed schist, the roches pourries, over old volcanic rock, rich in iron and manganese. Its Gamay is deeper and stonier than that of the granite crus. The Foillard domaine, fwah-YAR, at Villié-Morgon, farms vines from about ten to ninety years old and is certified organic.

It is made the old Beaujolais way, with whole bunches and native yeasts, and bottled without fining or filtering. 2024 was a wet year in Beaujolais, with mildew, hail and a small crop, and its reds came out fresh. The 2024 tastes of plum, red and black fruit, black tea and crushed stone, with light tannin and lively acidity.

It is on the list as the red for a large table ordering a bit of everything: light enough for poultry and mushrooms, with the depth for duck and pork.

value.a:
Asked: Is this like Beaujolais Nouveau?

Answer: No. Morgon is one of the ten crus, the top villages, and the Côte du Py is its best known hill; this is Gamay with depth that can age.

Asked: Why serve a red cool?

Answer: Gamay tastes brighter and fresher slightly cool, around 55 to 58°F.

Asked: What was 2024 like?

Answer: A wet year with mildew and a small crop; the wines are fresh and lively rather than big. A magnum is two bottles, ten to twelve glasses, and the sommelier can say how it shows tonight.

entries.target: wine:Diebolt-Vallois ‘Blanc de Blancs’ Extra Brut NV (1.5 L magnum)

value.a:
Diebolt-Vallois Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut is a non-vintage grower Champagne in magnum, $220 for 1.5 L, bin 32212, printed under Large Formats, Champagne and again under Champagne, Grower Producers, and the least expensive Champagne magnum on the list.

Diebolt-Vallois, dee-BOLT vah-LWAH, is a family grower in Cramant, a Grand Cru village of the Côte des Blancs, the chalk slope south of Épernay planted almost entirely with Chardonnay. The Blanc de Blancs is all Chardonnay, drawn from Cuis and Chouilly and neighboring villages. Cuis is a Premier Cru village, so the blend does not carry the Grand Cru name.

It is Extra Brut: the rules allow no more than six grams of sugar a liter at disgorging, and this one carries very little. It tastes of lemon with a salty, iodine edge, taut and very dry.

It is on the list as the Champagne magnum for a big table that starts with oysters and crab. A magnum is two bottles, ten to twelve glasses, and Champagne ages more slowly in it, with the same air under one cork for twice the wine.

value.a:
Asked: What is Extra Brut?

Answer: Drier than Brut: no more than six grams of sugar a liter, so it tastes very dry and lets the lemon and salt show.

Asked: What is grower Champagne?

Answer: Champagne made by the family that grows the grapes, here in Cramant, rather than by a house that buys most of its grapes.

Asked: Is it Grand Cru?

Answer: The family is in Cramant, a Grand Cru village, but this blend also draws on Cuis, a Premier Cru, so it does not carry the name. The magnum pours ten to twelve glasses.

lines.s10: A magnum of Lucien Crochet Sancerre rosé: pale, dry Pinot Noir, melon and blood orange, for the crudo and the tostada.
lines.s20: For a table that wants rosé, the Lucien Crochet magnum is Sancerre Pinot Noir from Bué, pressed straight away, so pale and dry: melon and blood orange with crisp acidity for the burnt orange and aguachile of the Tuna Crudo.
lines.s45: Sancerre is known for Sauvignon Blanc, but its red grape is Pinot Noir, and Lucien Crochet, a family estate in Bué, makes this rosé from it. The grapes are pressed straight away, so the juice takes only a pale blush from the skins, and the wine is dry. 2024 was wet in Sancerre, with mildew and a small crop, and its wines are light and crisp. This one tastes of melon and blood orange with an aniseed finish. Its acidity meets the tomato and burrata of the Creole Tomato Tostada and the burnt orange of the Tuna Crudo, and a magnum pours ten to twelve glasses.
lines.sale: Lucien Crochet is Sancerre rosé of Pinot Noir from Bué, pressed straight away: pale, dry, melon and blood orange, our only still rosé magnum. Offer it to a table of six sharing the Tuna Crudo and the Creole Tomato Tostada.

entries.target: wine:Lucien Crochet Sancerre Rosé 2024 (1.5 L magnum)

value.a:
Lucien Crochet Sancerre Rosé 2024 is a dry rosé of Pinot Noir in magnum, $185 for 1.5 L, bin 12262, printed under Large Formats, Rosé and again under Rosé, France, and the only still rosé in large format on the list; the other rosé magnums are Champagne.

Sancerre, sahn-SAIR, is the hilltop town of the upper Loire whose white is Sauvignon Blanc; its red grape is Pinot Noir, which makes its red and its rosé. Lucien Crochet, loo-SYAN kroh-SHAY, is a family estate in Bué, one of the appellation’s villages.

The rosé is all Pinot Noir, pressed straight away so the juice takes only a pale color from the skins, and fermented dry. 2024 was a hard, wet year in Sancerre, with mildew and a small crop, and its wines are light, crisp and moderate in alcohol. The 2024 tastes of melon and blood orange, crisp at the start, with an aniseed finish.

It is on the list for a large table that wants rosé with fish and tomatoes. A magnum is two bottles, ten to twelve glasses, and wine ages more slowly in it, with the same air under one cork for twice the wine.

value.a:
Asked: Is it sweet?

Answer: No. It is pale because the Pinot Noir was pressed straight away, with little time on the skins; color is no sign of sugar, and this rosé is dry.

Asked: Sancerre makes rosé?

Answer: Yes. Sancerre’s red grape is Pinot Noir, and it makes the appellation’s red and rosé.

Asked: Is it the 2024 or the 2025?

Answer: The magnum is the 2024; the 750 ml comes in both. The sommelier can say which is open tonight.

entries.target: wine:Lucien Crochet Sancerre Rosé 2024 (1.5 L magnum)

value.a: Present the magnum with both hands and say Lucien Crochet, Sancerre rosé, 2024, loo-SYAN kroh-SHAY. Serve it at 46 to 50°F in white-wine glasses from an ice bucket of ice and water; no decanting. Pour a taste for the host, then small pours so the magnum reaches every guest, the host last, with a hand under the base and the thumb in the punt. Say: “Crochet’s Sancerre rosé: melon and blood orange, pale and dry.”
